title: President Marcos to non-commissioned AFP officers: We stand behind you
summary: President Marcos has asked non-commissioned officers (NCOs) of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) to keep up the good work as he assured them of the government’s full support in the…

blocks.text: “As your commander-in-chief, I want you to know that just as you stand in defense of our nation, we will always stand behind you,” Marcos said on Facebook.

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos has asked non-commissioned officers (NCOs) of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) to keep up the good work as he assured them of the government’s full support in the performance of their duties.

Marcos joined the members of the AFP Council of Sergeants Major in a boodle fight at the General Headquarters Building in Camp General Emilio Aguinaldo, Quezon City, in celebration of the council’s 57th anniversary on Thursday.?
“So we, on our part, will provide all the support we can and indeed, we are well aware of the great importance of your work, of what you are doing,” Marcos said.?
The President recognized the invaluable contributions of NCOs in ensuring the operational effectiveness and continuity of leadership within the military establishment.
“The officers command the AFP. But the NCOs are the backbone of the military,” he added.?
He noted that the NCOs are responsible for translating orders into action and ensuring the successful execution of military operations.?
Marcos underscored their vital role in bridging the gap between commissioned officers and enlisted men and women, particularly younger military personnel.?
He acknowledged their responsibilities in preserving institutional memory and military traditions, recognizing outstanding personnel and assisting those experiencing difficulties.?
Marcos encouraged the NCOs to communicate openly with their superiors regarding the problems, concerns and needs of their troops.?
“When you see something that needs to be done or you see a problem or you hear something about the needs of our troops, please tell us all,” Marcos added.?
He said that every officer in the chain of command, must be informed about the conditions and welfare of military personnel.?
